text:
rachel: Quick follow-up after yesterday's RFC: proposal to move per-layer scale/zero-point maps into a separate artefact (scale-maps) instead of baking into the model quant blob. Keeps model bits stable while we iterate calibration.
tom: That would let us hot-swap calibration without changing model checksums, nice. Any perf cost from extra lookup?
rachel: Minimal. Runtime caches the active map per model instance and applies it during weight dequant. We measured ~0.5% throughput hit on p99 in microbenchmarks.
jin: Operationally we need to track which scale-map was used. Add map_id and map_hash into traces. Also provide an ancestry header: model_checksum -> map_id -> deployment_override.
mila: From quality POV we should introduce a "degrade_score" for each inference that is a tiny aggregator of token-confidence-shift + rerank delta. Not a perfect quality metric but gives us a signal for drifting calibrations.
rachel: Agree. Thinking of fields in the profile metadata: compatibility_enum (STRICT | RELAXED), fallback_chain (list: fp8,int8,4bit), max_permitted_degrade (float), monitor_window_secs (int).
jin: On fallback_chain: runtime must pick the first available compatible slot; ensure we can express headwise fallbacks e.g., "attn:fp8->int8,ffn:fp8->4bit". Maybe we need a small DSL for per-op directives.
tom: DSL increases complexity. Could we instead support per-component tags and a simple list of prioritized quant modes? Prefer smaller surface for now.
mila: +1 to prioritized list. We can add an advanced per-op field later if we see need.
qa-bot: Canary alert: profile scale-map map-2026-03-05 produced degrade_score mean=0.045 over 5m on prod-mnlf. Marking canary=fail and paging @rachel @jin.
rachel: Got it. I'll roll the canary back to map-2026-02-28 and schedule shadow runs for the revised calibration.
jin: One safety thought: add a runtime "fast-sim" check that replays a tiny canonical anchor (3 prompts) through the active map locally before accepting a map into canary. If fast-sim fails, reject. Cheap and catches obvious regressions.
tom: How do we prevent stale cached maps from lingering after a rollback? Add an eviction_ttl plus a grace_period for immediate invalidation.
mila: Also expose a /runtime/profile/check endpoint so SRE can query effective profile + map for a live worker. Useful during incidents.
qa-bot: Telemetry request: store per-map histograms of degrade_score, p99 latency, and a 10-sample anonymized output buffer for triage (with PII scrub).
jin: For signing and ownership: each map gets owner, signed_version, and approval_state (draft|shadow|canary|signed). Only signed maps allowed to be promoted to deployment overrides automatically.
rachel: Good. I'll update the RFC with these changes: separate scale-maps artefact, map metadata fields (map_id,map_hash,owner,signed_version,approval_state), compatibility_enum, fallback_chain, max_permitted_degrade, eviction_ttl, fast-sim gate, and the /runtime/profile/check contract. Will paste link when done.
tom: One more: add a lightweight header in responses like "x-quant-map-used: map-2026-02-28;degrade_score:-0.03" so callers can expose to downstream logging.
rachel: Nice small change, we'll add that. Thanks everyone.
